overview.description: Cucumber is a Nordic lose-last-trick game: the goal is to avoid winning the final trick of the hand.

history.origins: Cucumber appears in Nordic student card culture and is documented with national variants such as Agurk and Gurka.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Early documented forms in Scandinavian card books.
1970s-1980s: Popular student game across Denmark, Sweden, Finland and neighbors.
history.evolution: Regional variants alter the beat rule and scoring thresholds while keeping the lose-last-trick core.
history.cultural: Known for reverse-pressure trick play where high cards can become liabilities late.

setup.players: From 2 to 7 players in the baseline Danish form (Agurk); the Swedish variant Gurka allows 3 to 8, and some regional forms use extra decks for more. The game was popular with students across Nordic countries; this build uses the common 2–7 player range with seven cards each.
setup.equipment: Deck and score tracking for penalty totals.
setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards each in Danish Agurk baseline; undealt cards are set aside unseen.

rules.objective: Avoid winning the last trick of each hand; the player who takes the final trick receives penalty points. Stay below the elimination threshold (e.g. 21 or 30) and be the last player remaining.
rules.gameplay: Forehand leads first trick. On each play, a player must either play a card equal to or higher than the current highest card in the trick, or play their lowest card. Highest card (or last of equals) wins trick and leads next. Winner of the final trick takes the penalty.
keyRules: Lose-last-trick objective: final trick winner is penalized.
Beat-or-lowest rule governs legal play choices.
Highest rank wins trick; in ties, last played equal rank wins.
Penalty is typically the rank value of the losing last-trick card.
Many tables eliminate players at threshold score (for example 21 or 30).

strategy.basic: Dump dangerous high cards when possible before the final trick.
strategy.intermediate: Track which players still hold high ranks to avoid being trapped into winning trick seven.
strategy.advanced: Manipulate lead timing so opponents are forced into overtake-or-lowest dilemmas late.
tips: Holding both very high and very low cards gives better endgame flexibility.
Late-trick position strongly affects whether a tie-high can be forced onto another player.

list.name: Swedish Previous-Card Rule
list.description: Players may only need to beat the previous card played, not the current highest in trick.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change is procedural; no engine constant overrides needed for this variant.

list.name: Polish Ogorek Last-Trick Ace Low
list.description: In final trick, Ace counts as low (1) for penalty valuation.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Ace-low-in-last-trick is a rule variant; no engine constant overrides documented.

difficulty.easy: Plays greedy beat cards without long-term last-trick planning.
difficulty.medium: Balances immediate trick safety with hand-shaping for endgame.
difficulty.hard: Forecasts forced-play trees under beat-or-lowest constraints and minimizes expected last-trick loss.

considerations: Core solver objective is avoid final trick win, not maximize trick count.
Legal-move generator must enforce beat-or-lowest rule every play.

phases.notes: Beat highest or play lowest; trick winner leads next.

phases.label: Last Trick Penalty
phases.notes: Final trick winner receives penalty points.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
engine.dealPattern: Deal seven cards each; play seven tricks.

hero.title: CUCUMBER

hero.tagline: Do not take the final trick.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Nordic reverse trick game where winning the last trick is bad.

prompts.human: In Cucumber, avoid winning the final trick. Beat high cards when forced, but shape your hand for a safe ending.
prompts.ai: Game: Cucumber. Flow: deal 7, play 7 tricks under beat-or-lowest rule, assign penalty to final trick winner.

scoring.description: Penalty-point accumulation game; final trick winner receives points by card value in many variants.
scoring.winCondition: Stay below elimination threshold and avoid taking final tricks across deals.

penalties.last_trick: Final trick winner takes card-value penalty (common Agurk form).
